Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

Gov. Code § 84308: Parties to any proceeding involving a license, permit, or other entitlement for use pending before the City
Council must disclose any campaign contribution over $250 (aggregated) within the preceding 12 months made by the party, their
agent, and those required to be aggregated with their contributions under Gov. Code § 82015.5. The disclosure must include the
amount contributed and the name(s) of the contributor(s). "G.C. § 84308: Yes" on this agenda indicates that the item is subject to
these regulations.

  REGULAR MEETING

Vice Mayor Ayala called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. in the Council Chambers,
Norwalk City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to roll call
were Councilmembers Perez, Ramirez, and Valencia, and Vice Mayor Ayala. Mayor Rios
was absent. Also present were Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Gloria V. Ramirez,
Deputy City Attorney; and Theresa Devoy, City Clerk.

The invocation was delivered by Myrna Brito, Spirit Life Community Church; followed by
the flag salute, led by Hailee Garcia, Hutchinson Middle School.
 Minutes of the Closed Session and Regular Meetings
Norwalk City Council
June 18, 2024

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

The City Attorney indicated there was no reportable action taken on the matter discussed
in closed session.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Councilmember Perez congratulated former Mayor Mike Mendez on his two children’s
Broadway show performance at the Tony Awards and their continued success while
representing Norwalk; encouraged all to attend the Independence Day Celebration on
July 2 on the City Hall lawn; and shared that the City Council meeting of July 2 would be
cancelled as a result of the event.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

City Council recognized Mr. William Rivera for his First Aid Assistance to Senior Citizen.

City Council recognized Deputy Kelley for his Outstanding Service to Norwalk as Motor
Deputy.

City Council proclaimed July as Parks and Recreation month in the City of Norwalk.

City Council presented the Emergency Operations Division of Public Safety with a
California Emergency Services Association Silver Award.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

Mr. Gomez congratulated John Ramirez, Director of Community Development, on his
retirement and thanked him for his outstanding service to the City. Mr. Gomez announced
that although the Social Services facility will be closed for renovations during the month
of July, services will continue and staff will temporarily be relocated to City Hall and the
Senior Center. Allan Perdomo, Director of Recreation and Park Services, provided an
update on the Hermosillo Park renovation project. Videos highlighting the Norwalk 5K
Run and “Bi-Weekly Review” were shown. Addressing City Council was Jack Cornejo,
who spoke in support of the 5K Run.

DIRECTOR’S REPORT

John P. Ramirez, Director of Community Development, provided a report and shared a
video highlighting the Community Development department.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 24-39 - APPROVAL OF DISADVANTAGED BUSINESS
  ENTERPRISE THREE-YEAR GOAL FOR FEDERAL FISCAL YEARS 2025
  THROUGH 2027

Background:

Pursuant to Federal Regulation 49 CFR Part 26 - Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE); all
public agencies receiving U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) funds, that anticipate
awarding $250,000 or more in USDOT-assisted contracts, must establish a three-year overall
DBE goal for potential contracting opportunities for certified Suppliers.

The purpose of the Triennial DBE Goal is to level the playing field for DBEs to compete in
obtaining USDOT assisted contracts. Therefore, Norwalk Transit System (NTS), as a Federal
Transit Administration (FTA) recipient has established a three percent (3%) Triennial DBE goal
using race neutral (0.91%) and race conscious (2.09%) measures, specifically using DBE
contract goals in awarding various FTA funded contracts and must meet the maximum feasible
portion of this goal.

A three percent (3%) base figure was calculated based on an analysis of DBE availability (See
Attachment A).

Race-neutral solicitation includes but is not limited to: (1) arranging contracts in ways to facilitate
small business participation such as unbundling large contracts or requiring prime contractors
to subcontract portions of the work; (2) providing bonding, financing, and technical assistance;
(3) communicating contract opportunities to the small business community; or (4) providing
business support and development services.
 City Council  July 16, 2024
Resolution No. 24-38 DBE Triennial Goal  Page No. 2

Race-conscious solicitation includes establishing a contract goal that focuses specifically on
utilizing DBEs, including minority and women owned DBEs. As such, the prime contractor must
affirm that they will meet the DBE goal set in their contract. If they fail to meet their goal, then
they must prove that they conducted good faith efforts to utilize DBEs.

The overall goal must reflect the level of DBE participation absent the effects of
discrimination. The overall goal is determined from an examination of DBE baseline availability
in the recipient’s region and local market, using DBE directory information, census data, bidders’
lists, disparity or similar studies, historical information, and data on local market conditions.

Fiscal Impact:

There is no material budget impact in the administration and implementation of this federally
mandated DBE program. However, for the three-year period of Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-2027, NTS
anticipates awarding $7,520,091 in contracting opportunities assisted in whole or in part with
FTA capital funds.

Citizens Advised:

On June 7, 2024, a public notice inviting comment on the recommended DBE goal for FY 2025-
2027 was published in The Norwalk Patriot, posted on the Transportation page of the City’s
website as well as each of the City’s designated posting locations. There have been no
comments received to date.

Strategic Plan 2023 Implementation:

N/A

  I. INTRODUCTION

The Norwalk Transit System (hereinafter referred to as “NTS”) is required to develop and submit
a Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE) Overall Goal for DBE participation as a condition of
receiving federal assistance, pursuant to 49 CFR Part 26 “Participation by Disadvantaged
Business Enterprises in U.S. Department of Transportation Programs” and the Federal Transit
Administration (FTA) Master Funding Agreement.

  II. BACKGROUND

NTS is a recipient of USDOT, Federal Transit Administration (FTA), funding. As a condition of
receiving this assistance, NTS signed an assurance that it will comply with FTA DBE
requirements. In accordance with Title 49 CFR Part 26 provisions, NTS is required to develop
and submit an overall Triennial DBE Goal for its FTA-assisted projects.

NTS herein presents its Proposed Overall DBE Goal Methodology for FFY 2025-27 goal period,
which resulted in a 3% Overall DBE Goal (.91% Race Neutral/ 2.09% Race Conscious).

  III. DOT-ASSISTED CONTRACTING PROGRAM FOR FFY 2025-2027

Market Area
The Federal DBE Program requires agencies to implement the DBE Program based on
information from the relevant geographic market area—the area in which the agency spends the
substantial majority of its contracting dollars. NTS’s local market for contracts consists of a
geographic area that is:

  • Where a large majority of contracting dollars is expended, and
  • Where a substantial number of contractors and subcontractors are located and
  available to submit bids, quotes, or proposals.

NTS’s bidder’s list was also reviewed and analyzed to determine where NTS spends the
substantial majority of its contracting dollars. This analysis confirmed that the previously
recognized market area of Los Angeles, Orange and San Bernardino counties is still valid.

triennial period and were considered in preparing this goal methodology. These projects and
their federal share of funding are listed in Table 1. The project scopes vary and include Transit
Facility, Tenant and Security Improvements, Maintenance Agreements for NTS Buses and
Vehicles, Software and Hardware procurements. All of NTS’s Projects have been grouped by

VIII. EVIDENCE FROM STUDIES

NTS did not find it feasible to conduct a its own independent availability/disparity study;
however, Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) identified two disparity studies,
inclusive of market areas like NTS’, to consider whether a Race-Conscious DBE Program
should continue to be implemented. The two identified disparity studies were the Caltrans
Disparity Study and the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro)
Disparity Study.

Caltrans FTA disparity study was completed in August 2022. This study focused on professional
services and goods, non-professional service contracts and procurements that Caltrans
awarded between October 1st, 2017, through September 30th, 2020. The overall FTA DBE
Goal for the relative availability of DBEs in Caltrans FTA 2022 Disparity Study was 6.3 percent
(6.3%). Caltrans’ FTA Disparity Study included thousands of contracts from areas outside of the
NTS market area as well as projects that had minimal relation to the contract scopes included
for NTS and therefore NTS opted to not utilize Caltrans FTA Disparity Study when considering
an adjustment to their base figure or their current race-neutral DBE application measures.

The second disparity study taken into consideration was Metro’s Disparity Study due to the
similarities in the market area and timeliness of the contracts reviewed. Where the Caltrans
Study market area included the entire state of California, the Metro Disparity Study focused on
Los Angeles County which is more aligned with NTS’s market area. The Metro Disparity Study
included a five-year study period (January 1, 2016 through December 31, 2021) to determine
any differences between the participation of minority- and woman-owned businesses in relevant
contracts and the availability of those businesses to perform that work (referred to as
disparities). Disparity analysis results indicated that most racial/ethnic and gender groups
showed disparities on contracts where race- and gender-conscious measures were not in place
during the study period. As a result, the disparity study recommended the use of contract DBE
goals.

As Metro’s Disparity Study satisfies the legal standards established by the Ninth Circuit Court of
Appeals in Western States Paving Co., Inc. v. Washington State Department of Transportation,
and guidance from the U.S. DOT/FTA concerning the implementation of race-conscious
application, NTS has elected to utilize this study as a basis for continuing to implement the race-
conscious component of their Overall DBE goal. NTS will ensure that the use of Race-
Conscious goals is narrowly tailored and consistent with other relevant legal standards.

NTS will continue to review applicable disparity studies as they become available and apply the
appropriate adjustments to their Race-Neutral/Race-Conscious DBE goal application.

agencies in development, construction and/or acquisition of land for school sites, airport
expansion, outdoor billboard signs, cell sites, retail shopping centers, golf course communities,
hotels and resorts, storage facilities, corporation yards, auto body shop, car washes and single-
family homes. During the past 25 years, TRA has assisted many public agencies, including
cities, counties, state, school districts and Federal agencies throughout California with their
strategic real estate needs, including: the development of public service buildings, negotiating
and structuring acquisitions, sales and property exchanges, providing asset management
solutions and interfacing with developers, community groups and other property owners to
originate and implement mutually beneficial results for both. In addition, they provide expert
witness and development consultant services for Caltrans in real estate matters, and have
extensive experience in eminent domain matters.

On June 4, 2018 the City entered into an agreement with TRA to provide development and
construction services for outdoor billboard signs. The services included, among other tasks, the
following tasks: a base map of existing billboard signs on interstates, a short report on
opportunities and constraints for each identified site (existing and proposed) with strategies for
each and a base map of existing billboard signs on surface streets. A priority list of locations for
new digital LED billboard signs with a timeline and schedule to obtain approvals for each and
work with a sign company to develop, construct, and operate a new LED sign was also
provided. Furthermore, TRA assisted in developing and implementing a Development
Agreement with Evergreen Media, as well as interfaced with Caltrans Outdoor Advertising
Division regarding the permitting process for the Firestone Billboard. On September 21, 2021,
 City Council  July 16, 2024

City Council approved an Agreement with TRA to continue providing development and
construction services for digital billboards.

Staff is seeking City Council authorization to continue to work with TRA to provide the following
services: including but not limited continue to negotiating a lease or other conveyance for a sign
on the existing DoubleTree Hotel property to develop a new digital LED sign, working with the
City and Primestor for The Walk, developing business aspects for other identified sites for
potential pylon signs, assisting with the creation of a new sign district, working with City staff
and the City Attorney on the business aspects for all identified sites for potential signs,
negotiating development agreements or leases, and soliciting interest from qualified sign
companies; and assisting City staff in real property and sign matters as-needed.

Fiscal Impact:

The Fiscal Year 2024/25 Budget includes $50,000 of RDA bond proceeds for contract
services. No general fund impact is anticipated.

SUBJECT:  DELINQUENT EMERGENCY BOARD-UP COLLECTION FEES

Background:

Whenever unsafe conditions are found to create a hazard to safety, health or public welfare, by
reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, fire hazard, disaster damage, vandalism or
abandonment, staff takes an emergency action to secure or otherwise abate the hazardous
conditions to protect the public. The property owner on record is sent an invoice of the costs
incurred by the City for this process. Unpaid invoices are processed as a special assessment
to the property.

Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) §15.32.150A specifies: “all buildings or structures which are
structurally unsafe or not provided with adequate egress, or which constitute a fire hazard, or
are otherwise dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use constitute a hazard
to safety or health or public welfare, by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation,
obsolescence, fire hazard, disaster damage, or abandonment, as specified in this Code or in
any other effective ordinance or statute, are, for the purpose of this section, unsafe buildings
and constitute an unsafe condition. All such unsafe buildings or conditions are hereby declared
to be public nuisances and shall be abated by repair, rehabilitation, improvement, removal, or
demolition, in whole or part, in accordance with the procedures specified in this code.”

NMC §15.32.170 specifies: “when any unoccupied building or structure is not properly secured,
locked or closed and is accessible to juveniles, transients, and unauthorized persons and is a
health and/or safety hazard to the adjacent community, the Building Official shall serve the
record owner and (if not the owner) the person having control of such building or structure with
a notice to secure or close the same forthwith so as to prevent unauthorized persons from
gaining access thereto.”
 City Council  July 16, 2024
Delinquent Emergency Board-up Collection Fees  Page No. 2

NMC §15.32.170.12 establishes emergency procedures: “whenever in the opinion of the
Building Official the conditions described in Section 15.32.170 constitute such an immediate
hazard that access to the building or structure must be limited or closed forthwith or within less
than the designated period, or either the Sheriff, Public Safety Director, or Chief of the Fire
Department so finds and so notifies the Building Official, he or she shall limit access to such
building after giving such notice to the record owner or the person in charge, or both as the
circumstances will permit or without any notice whatever when, in the opinion of the Building
Official, Sheriff, Public Safety Director, or the Chief of the Fire Department, immediate action is
necessary.”

A “Declaration of Substandard” is filed with the Los Angeles County Recorder’s Office as part of
the nuisance abatement process to notify interested parties of the pending cost associated with
the abatement.

Discussion:

Notice of the abatement expenses are sent as an invoice to the property owners of record. Staff
keeps an accounting of the abatement expenses associated with each property. Attached is an
itemized summary showing the outstanding costs to date. Property owners were mailed the
required 45-day notice of the proposed lien assessment for these unpaid board up costs, which
allows owners to bring objections over their property assessments before the Property
Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Board (Board).

Also attached is a list of properties that were invoiced for emergency board-up work performed
in Fiscal Years (FY) 2022/23 and 2023/24 pursuant to Chapter 15.32 of the NMC for which
reimbursement has not been received, in the amount of $14,796.23.

On June 26, 2024, the Property Maintenance and Rehabilitation Appeals Board (Board)
conducted a hearing to consider a report on the properties with delinquent charges and to hear
objections of any property owner liable to be assessed for the costs of emergency board up
work.

The Board, by a 4-0 vote, recommended that the listed properties be assessed for the
emergency board ups unless the outstanding balance is paid prior to August 1, 2024.

Fiscal Impact:

Revenue from the collection of delinquent emergency board-up collection fees is included in the
proposed Fiscal Year 2022/23 and 2023/24 Budget.

SUBJECT:  DELINQUENT REFUSE COLLECTION ACCOUNTS

Background:

Norwalk Municipal Code Section 8.48.280, Mandatory Service, requires all solid waste collected
from residential, commercial, or industrial premises for a fee, service charge, or other
consideration, shall be collected by a solid waste enterprise under the provisions of an exclusive
contract awarded by City Council.

City procedures state that any owner who has a delinquent account during the period of May 1,
2023 to April 30, 2024 shall be sent, by mail, written notification that the Property Maintenance
and Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board (Appeals Board) will review all such delinquent
accounts during a public hearing.

Summary:

Approximately 2,493 notices for accounts that were delinquent as of April 30, 2024 were mailed
on May 1, 2024, totaling $436,068. Since the original lists were prepared, many payments or
adjustments have been processed and removed from the delinquent account list. The Appeals
Board conducted a public hearing on June 26, 2024 and recommended that City Council move
to lien the listed properties, with the exception of those customers that have resolved their
accounts by the July 31, 2024 deadline. Daily payments and/or adjustments will continue to be
processed through July 31, 2024. If approved by City Council, action will be taken to submit the
delinquent charges, including the $25 per account City administrative fee, to the Los Angeles
County Tax Collector for placement on the 2024 property tax bill.

Fiscal Impact:

The City will be reimbursed $25 per account for administrative costs. The total amount will not
be known until the final list is completed.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT FOR PUBLIC HOUSING AGENCY PLANS CONTINUED
  HOUSING ASSISTANCE AND THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK
  GRANT AND HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIP PROGRAMS 2025/30
  CONSOLIDATED PLAN, FIRST YEAR ANNUAL ACTION PLAN, UPDATED
  ANALYSIS OF IMPEDIMENTS TO FAIR HOUSING CHOICE AND A HOUSING
  SUMMIT

Background:

The Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships
Program (HOME) are funded by the United States Department of Housing and Urban
Development (HUD), and every five years a Five-Year Consolidated Plan (Plan) and First Year
Annual Action Plan (AAP) is required as part of the annual application process that must be
submitted for funding. For reference the current Five-Year Consolidated Plan covers the time
period: July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2025.

The Plan lists the specific activities that the City will undertake with the CDBG and HOME
funds. The types of activities that the City may conduct are subject to federal rules and
regulations, such as funding caps on program administration and social services, requirements
for public-private partnerships, and compliance with National Objectives.

The Consolidated Plan submission must also include an Analysis of Impediments to Fair
Housing Choice (AI). The AI focuses on actions, omissions and decisions made which restrict,
or have the effect of restricting, housing choices or the availability of housing choices on the
basis of race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status or national origin in the City of Norwalk.
Such actions may include lending decisions, real estate advertising, discrimination in rental
housing, hate crimes and zoning requirements.
 City Council  July 16, 2024
Agreement for Public Housing Agency Plans  Page No. 2

Michael Baker International (MBI) currently provides professional services to the Norwalk
Housing Authority (NHA) with the preparation of the Public Housing Agency (PHA) Plans and
the continued operation and management of the various HUD funded Housing Authority
Programs. The PHA Administrative plan is a comprehensive guide to the PHA policies,
programs, operations, and strategies for meeting the City’s housing needs goals. To ensure
deliverable (tasks) associated with operations and reporting are performed in a timely fashion
and compliant with all federal regulations, the NHA depends on MBI for guidance and assistance
with the following tasks: NHA Administrative Plan, Five-Year Consolidated Plan Project Based
Voucher (PBV) contracts.

Timeline for deliverables

The draft AI is to be made available for public review and comment for a period of 30 days
starting July 2024. After the public review period, the final AI will be presented to City Council
in August 2024 for information purposes. A Housing Summit scheduled for September 6, 2024,
and ongoing data collection tasks such as, stakeholder outreach and interviews to be conducted
through December 2024. The first draft of the Consolidated Plan is due to staff by January 2025.
The final Plan is due to HUD on May 15, 2025.

MBI submitted a proposal to prepare the Consolidated Plan, AAP, and updated AI based on
pertinent requirements of HUD. The proposal includes providing comprehensive professional
consulting services required for the successful and timely preparation of the Consolidated Plan,
the AI and the first-year AAP at costs that fall within the annual planning and administrative fees
allowed by HUD. Based on the strength of their housing team and expertise, MBI was retained
by the City.

During the contract term with MBI, their housing team assigned to performed work on the
housing tasks for the City transitioned to MNS Engineers. Therefore, staff is proposing to secure
services with MNS Engineers for continuity and institutional knowledge and the fact that the City
has critical milestones that would be jeopardized if the consultants cannot continue the
necessary CDBG, HOME and Housing tasks. The project team is well qualified to provide the
services and have a combined 80+ years of housing and community development experience.

Staff has reviewed MNS Engineers scope and find their selection will provide for a seamless
transition during this critical period. In addition, per CFR 24 85.36 staff is permitted to make a
change in consultant services for a maximum 12-month period if an emergency exists. In this
case the transition of critical housing staff from MBI to MNS Engineers is justification for such a
recommendation from staff. CFR also requires the City to procure housing consulting services
in the future following solicitation methods in accordance with all applicable local, state and
federal guidelines for procurement of professional services. The Request for Proposal (RFP) is
expected to be released early in 2025 to retain a new consultant by June 2025.
 City Council  July 16, 2024

The NHA, CDBG and HOME programs are funded solely by the United States Department of

SUBJECT:  ORDINANCE NO. 24-1747 – ZONING TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2024-01 TO
  AMEND VARIOUS SECTIONS OF TITLE 17 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL
  CODE AS IT RELATES TO SPECIFIC PLAN AREA NO. 1

Background:

The Specific Plan Area No. 1 (SPA 1) was adopted by Ordinance No. 1267 in 1987, in order to
establish objectives, policies, regulations, development standards, and review criteria for the
implementation of a compatible blend of mutually supporting land uses consisting of a multi-
story hotel, a wide array of professional offices and retail commercial uses, complementary
commercial entertainment uses, and residential condominiums.

This City staff-initiated proposal, Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) No. 2024-01, amends various
sections of Title 17 (Zoning) of the Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) as it relates to Article 1,
SPA 1.

On June 26, 2024, the Planning Commission conducted a duly noticed public hearing on the
aforementioned project and with a 4-0 vote, recommended approval to City Council for Zoning
Text Amendment (ZTA) No. 2024-01. There were public comments at the public hearing
expressing concerns with the proposed action. An email and letter, Attachment 4, from Attorney,
Jordan R. Sisson, on behalf of Unite Here 11, were submitted for the record. In summary, the
concerns were as follows:

  •  The SPA1 Zoning Text Amendment excludes mention of a 121-room hotel, and the
  Amendment should include the project-specific entitlement;
  •  Adequacy of California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review for the action, as the
  Common-Sense Exemption is not applicable since the original SPA 1 did not contemplate
  a second hotel;
 City Council  July 16, 2024
Ordinance No. 24-1747 - ZTA No. 2024-01  Page No. 2

  •  Why the City is not considering additional uses or if a hotel is considered, a hotel specific
  development agreement requirement should be required; and
  •  Affordable Housing as an alternative to a potential hotel.

Staff responded to the comments made by the public. The Director of Community Development
described that the purpose of the ZTA was to create greater consistency and synergy with the
Entertainment District on the City Hall site which will include 360 housing units with 15% in
affordable housing. Additionally, the Director cited the City’s commitment to housing of varying
types including projects under construction such as Mercy Housing (60 veteran units),
collaborating with Los Angeles County and the Weingart Foundation for a Project Home Key
Site (51 units, housing voucher program). In addition, he stated there are approximately 1,500
to 1,700 units in construction, under consideration, approved, or on the verge of being approved.
He added that the major impediment to affordable housing is borrowing costs, as well as the
cost of land and materials, but the City is working creatively to overcome those barriers and
provide more housing choices to the community.

The Director indicated that the original SPA 1 contemplated an office building adjacent to the
hotel. He indicated there was consideration for a new second hotel behind the DoubleTree, but
that it was conceptual only and for any project to move forward a submittal would be necessary.
Any submittal would be evaluated in the future as needed. He added that there are concerns
with providing housing so close to the freeway such as health impacts that increase dramatically
when residents are within 500’ – 1000’ of the freeway and in this case the focus was on creating
housing further away.

Discussion

The request consists of ZTA No. 2024-01 to amend various sections of Title 17 of the NMC as
it relates to SPA 1 by allowing for a second hotel, expanding the list of allowable uses to include
billboards, arcades, and similar uses, updating the list of prohibited uses, establishing a
wayfinding signage review and approval process, and streamlining the entitlement process for
certain projects in SPA 1.

Pursuant to the CEQA, this project is exempt pursuant to CEQA Guidelines 15061(b)(3)
(Common Sense Exemption), where it can be seen with certainty there is no possibility that the
activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment. The project will not involve
any construction nor have a significant effect on the environment.

N/A

That the Planning Commission:

  Amendment (ZTA) No. 2024-01; and
2. Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption), where
  it can be seen with certainty there is no possibility that the activity in question may have
  significant effect of the environment.

AUTHORITY

Section 65855 of the California Government Code states that the Planning Commission shall
make a written recommendation on the adoption or amendment of the Zoning Ordinance.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2
Zoning Text Amendment No. 2024-01  June 26, 2024

Section 17.02.260.D of the NMC stipulates that the Planning Commission render its
recommendation on a Zoning Text Amendment, including the reasons for the
recommendation, to the City Council.

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

The SPA 1 was adopted by Ordinance No. 1267 in 1987, in order to establish objectives,
policies, regulations, development standards and review criteria for the implementation of a
compatible blend of mutually supporting land uses consisting of a multi-story hotel, a wide
array of professional offices and retail commercial uses, complementary commercial
entertainment uses and residential condominiums.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The request consists of ZTA No. 2024-01 to amend various sections of Title 17 (Zoning) of
the NMC as it relates to Article 1, SPA 1.

The proposed text amendments to SPA 1 will allow for up to two (2) hotels, modify the list of
allowable uses to include billboards and other uses, include minor text amendments to
include references to wayfinding and building identification signage, remove subsection
outlining roles and procedures for the final decision-making authority to streamline the
entitlement process and promote economic development.

ANALYSIS

SPA 1 is an area of critical importance to the long-term future of Norwalk due to its location,
size, ownership and potential where maximum effort is necessary to capitalize on these
opportunities. The proposed project is consistent with the objective of SPA 1 and anticipated
to expand development opportunities in the area. The proposed text amendments are
necessary in effectuating and facilitating such opportunities by updating the list of uses,
allowing for certain signage, and streamlining the entitlement process within SPA 1.

Zoning Text Amendment

The text amendment consists of the following components:

•  Allow for a second hotel. Currently, SPA 1 limits the number of hotels to only one. The
  inclusion of a second hotel provides greater flexibility and allows for additional
  development opportunities.

•  Expand the allowable uses to include, but not limited to: billboards, arcades, bowling alley,
  entertainment venues, museums, outdoor events, restaurants, lounges and clubs.
  Currently, SPA 1 prohibits billboards. The proposed language will allow for a billboard
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 3
Zoning Text Amendment No. 2024-01  June 26, 2024

  and include new uses that complement the existing establishments within SPA 1 and will
  enhance the appeal and attraction of the area for economic development opportunities.

•  The proposed text amendment will update the list of prohibited uses to remove uses that
  are outdated or inconsistent with the objective of SPA 1. These uses include: collection
  agencies, credit services, detective and protective services, manufacturing and
  commercial services, security and commodity brokers, dealers and exchanges, tax
  consultation, and telephone answering service.

•  Minor text amendments will include references to wayfinding (directional) and building
  identification signage. Wayfinding and modifications to on premise and off premise
  wayfinding signage will be allowed through the Director Approval Request (DAR) process.

•  The proposed text amendment will simplify and streamline the entitlement process by
  modifying the roles and procedures for final decision-making authority which will further
  facilitate development.

Public Notification

Notice of this public hearing was published in The Norwalk Patriot and posted at the City’s
three designated posting sites and the city website on June 14, 2024.

ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

 The project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption), where it can be seen
with certainty there is no possibility that the activity in question may have significant effect of
the environment.

SUMMARY

The proposed ZTA, which involves modifying SPA 1 and related provisions from the NMC,
will allow for a second hotel, allow for a billboard and additional compatible uses, remove
outdated uses, delineate an approval process for wayfinding signage and streamline the
entitlement approval process to encourage healthy development in a timely manner. SPA 1
is of critical importance to the long-term viability of Norwalk whereby it is critical to continue to
facilitate and encourage economic development opportunities in the area. Therefore, Staff
recommends that the Planning Commission recommend approval of the project to City
Council.

On behalf of UNITE HERE Local 11 (“Local 11”), please carefully review the attached comments
regarding the proposed Zoning Text Amendments (“ZTA(s)”) related to the 20-acre area known as
Specific Plan Area 1 (“SPA 1”). In short, Local 11 has several concerns with the proposed ZTAs, which

  3. WHY IS THE CITY NOT CONSIDERING ADDITIONAL USES—LIKE HOUSING—OR GREATER PROTECTIONS
  AROUND HOTEL DEVELOPMENTS –LIKE A HOTEL-SPECIFIC DA REQUIREMENT

  Currently, the SPA 1 allows “residential condominiums” in some areas of the SPA 1. (NMC §
  17.09.090; see also Fig. 4 above.) While the ZTA increases flexibility for commercial uses (e.g., hotel,
  retail, entertainment), it does not allow any increased flexibility for residential uses, like allowing
  housing throughout the plan area maximizing affordable housing. Under the City’s recently adopted
  2021-2029 Housing Element (“Housing Element”),15 the City has a Regional Housing Needs
  Allocation (“RHNA”) of approximately 5,000 units, with roughly 60 percent of the units needing to
  be affordable at moderate-income levels or lower. (See Housing Element, p. 175.) In light of the high
  need for housing (particularly affordable), it seems that the City should reconsider the best and
  highest use of the Site—such as a mixed-use housing development. Furthermore, the City should
  consider more protections over hotels, not fewer protections than those minimal limits adopted
  nearly 40 years ago. To address impacts caused by any future hotel project and ensure maximum
  public benefits, the City should consider making hotel use contingent on entering into a hotel-
  specific Development Agreement (“DA”) pursuant to Gov. Code § 65865 et. seq., as done by other
  cities or disallowing hotel use in this area.16

  In conclusion, the proposed ZTA is a project-specific SPA amendment that does not qualify
  for a Common-Sense exemption under CEQA. Local 11 respectfully requests that the Planning
  Commission deny the entire action until the issues discussed above are adequately addressed,

Background:

A Special Sign District is an overlay containing multiple parcels reasonably grouped together
that would allow for the approval of a freestanding sign. Freestanding signs are desirable to the
City of Norwalk (“City”) as they provide opportunities to enhance the urban aesthetics and
promote effective communication through controlled and cohesive signage.

City staff-initiated proposal, Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) No. 2024-02, establishes a city-wide
review process and regulatory framework for the creation of a Special Sign District. This item
will be considered concurrently with Zone Change No. 2024-01 and Zone Text Amendment No.
2024-03, a request to approve the Special Sign District No. 1 (SD 1) overlay and SD 1
development standards.

On June 26th, 2024, the Planning Commission recommended that City Council approve ZTA
No. 2024-02 and adopt Ordinance No. 24-1748 by a vote of 4-0. There were some in attendance
stating concerns about this action. An email and a letter from Jordon R. Sisson, Esq., an attorney
for Unite Here Local 11, were submitted to the record.

In summary their concerns were as follows:
  1. Adequacy of CEQA reviewed for the action.
  2. Concern that this action will allow for more projects, i.e. digital billboard signs, other
  accessory signs, etc.

Staff rebutted points raised by the opposition as follows:

of their submittal.

The request consists of ZTA No. 2024-02 to amend Title 17 (Zoning), Chapter 17.02 (Approval

appropriate zoning, types of uses and a review process to create a Special Sign District.

Pursuant to the CEQA, this project is exempt pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California

Section 17.02.260.D of the NMC stipulates that the Planning Commission render its
recommendation on a Zoning Text Amendment, including the reasons for the
recommendation, to the City Council.

  INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

  A Special Sign District is an effective Planning tool and serves as an overlay containing
  multiple parcels reasonably grouped together that would allow for the approval of a
  freestanding sign. Freestanding signs are desirable to the City of Norwalk (“City”) as they
  provide opportunities to enhance the urban aesthetics and promote effective
  communication through controlled and cohesive signage and to provide a reasonable and
  effective means of business promotion in areas where unique constraints in the built or
  natural environment exist.

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION

  City staff-initiated proposal, ZTA No. 2024-02, establishes a review process for the
  creation of a Special Sign District. A Special Sign District must include multiple parcels
  reasonably grouped together. Development standards for the sign(s) shall be
  incorporated within the Special Sign District’s Ordinance. The proposal requires the
  following minimum requirements:

  ·  Shall only include parcels within Specific Plan Area (SPA) 1, SPA 16, mixed-use,
  commercial, institutional and public facility overlay zone districts;

  ·  Minimum combined land area shall be five (5) acres;

  ·  Parcels shall be contiguous (but may be separated by a railroad or public street); and

  ·  Existing Uses shall include one (1) or more of the following: vehicle sales and lease
  (general new and used), hotels and motels (with 100 or more rooms) or a retail tenant
  (with a minimum area of 10,000 square feet).

  There are no specific sign guidelines established with this proposal. Sign design
  guidelines will be reviewed when a Special Sign District request is received. The review
  and approval process for a proposed Special Sign District requires approval by City
  Council.

  ANALYSIS

  3. WHY IS THE CITY NOT CONSIDERING ADDITIONAL USES—LIKE HOUSING—OR GREATER PROTECTIONS
  AROUND HOTEL DEVELOPMENTS –LIKE A HOTEL-SPECIFIC DA REQUIREMENT

  Currently, the SPA 1 allows “residential condominiums” in some areas of the SPA 1. (NMC §
  17.09.090; see also Fig. 4 above.) While the ZTA increases flexibility for commercial uses (e.g., hotel,
  retail, entertainment), it does not allow any increased flexibility for residential uses, like allowing
  housing throughout the plan area maximizing affordable housing. Under the City’s recently adopted
  2021-2029 Housing Element (“Housing Element”),15 the City has a Regional Housing Needs
  Allocation (“RHNA”) of approximately 5,000 units, with roughly 60 percent of the units needing to
  be affordable at moderate-income levels or lower. (See Housing Element, p. 175.) In light of the high
  need for housing (particularly affordable), it seems that the City should reconsider the best and
  highest use of the Site—such as a mixed-use housing development. Furthermore, the City should
  consider more protections over hotels, not fewer protections than those minimal limits adopted
  nearly 40 years ago. To address impacts caused by any future hotel project and ensure maximum
  public benefits, the City should consider making hotel use contingent on entering into a hotel-
  specific Development Agreement (“DA”) pursuant to Gov. Code § 65865 et. seq., as done by other
  cities or disallowing hotel use in this area.16

  In conclusion, the proposed ZTA is a project-specific SPA amendment that does not qualify
  for a Common-Sense exemption under CEQA. Local 11 respectfully requests that the Planning
  Commission deny the entire action until the issues discussed above are adequately addressed,
  including submission of all entitlement requested for the 121-room hotel in a CEQA-compliant
  analysis.

  A. Purpose. This Subsection sets forth regulations for the establishment of
  Special Sign Districts in areas of the City containing multiple parcels that
  may be reasonably grouped, the unique characteristics of which can be
  enhanced by the imposition of special sign guidelines and standards
  designed to enhance the theme or unique qualities of a certain area, or
  which reinforce the identity of certain areas of the City to promote business
  and strengthen the City’s tax base and to implement the General Plan.
  B. Establishment of Special Sign Districts. The City Council, the Planning
  Commission or the Community Development Director may initiate
  consideration of a proposed Ordinance to establish a Special Sign District
  as set forth in Section 17.02.290 (Zone Changes) of this Title. Special Sign
  Districts shall be considered an overlay zone to modify the underlying
  zoning district with regards to signage regulations, specifically with regards
  to freestanding signs.
  Page 5 of 6
 C. General requirements. All signs displayed in a Special Sign District shall
  comply with the provisions of this Chapter, except as set for this in this
  Subsection.
E. Minimum requirements:
  1. Zoning. Shall only include parcels in Specific Plan Area 1, Specific Plan
  Area 16, mixed-use, commercial, institutional and public facility overlay
  zoning districts. Shall not include parcels in residential zoning districts.
  2. Land area. The minimum area shall be five (5) acres.
  3. Land configuration. Shall include contiguous parcels of land, which may
  only be separated by a railroad or public street.
  4. Anchor business/tenant. The Special Sign District shall be one (1) or
  more of the following uses: vehicle sales and lease (general new and
  used), hotels and motels (with 100 and more rooms) or a retail tenant
  (with a minimum area of 10,000 square feet).
  5. Development standards. All development standards shall be determined
  at the time the Special Sign District is established and incorporated
  within the Special Sign District’s Ordinance.

SUBJECT:  ORDINANCE NO. 24-1749 - ZONE CHANGE NO. 2024-01 AND ORDINANCE
  NO. 24-1750 - ZONING TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2024-03, TO AMEND
  VARIOUS SECTIONS OF TITLE 17 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE AS
  IT RELATES TO SPECIAL SIGN DISTRICT NO. 1

Background:

In 2023, City Council adopted the Norwalk Entertainment District - Civic Center Specific Plan
Area 16 (SPA 16). SPA 16 is located at the southeast corner of Imperial Highway and Norwalk
Boulevard in Norwalk. The development of this area is anticipated to be implemented through
one or more leases to a private developer of all or a portion of the portion of the City owned land
and other contractual arrangements between the City and a private developer. Specific Plan
Area 1 (SPA 1) is located to the south of SPA 16. The SPA 1 parcels included in this proposal
comprise the AMC Theater, retail pad tenants and the Outback Steakhouse. Currently there is
one existing freestanding sign located in Assessor Parcel No. 8047-007-191, (the Outback
Steakhouse).

The height and location of the existing freestanding sign is not optimal given the existing
conditions. Establishing the proposed Special Sign District No. 1 (SD 1) will allow for the
relocation of the existing on-premise sign with a taller freeway oriented freestanding sign and
provide greater flexibility for businesses entities within the Norwalk Entertainment District (SPA
16) to utilize the sign, when submitted as part of their future Master Sign Program.

City staff-initiated, Zone Change (ZC) No. 2024-01 and Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) No.
2024-03, are a request to approve the Special Sign District No. 1 (SD 1) overlay and SD 1 sign
development standards. This item is to be considered concurrently with Zoning Text Amendment
(ZTA) No. 2024-02, a request to establish a review process and regulatory framework to allow
the creation of Special Sign Districts city wide. As set forth in ZTA No. 2024-02, a Special Sign

dependent on the approval and adoption of ZTA 2024-02.

On June 26, 2024, the Planning Commission conducted a duly noticed public hearing on the
aforementioned project and with a 4-0 vote, recommended approval to City Council for ZC No.
2024-01 and ZTA No. 2024-03.

There were some in attendance stating concerns with this action. An email and letter from
Jordon R. Sisson, Esq., an attorney for Unite Here Local 11, was submitted to the record.

In summary the concerns are as follows:
  1. Adequacy of California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) reviewed for the action.
  2. Concern that this action will allow for more projects; i.e. digital billboard sign, other
  accessory signs, etc.

Staff rebutted points raised by the opposition as follows:
  1. Staff confirmed the request is not in conjunction with any active application to construct
  a second hotel in SP 1, a billboard, or freestanding sign. Any future submittal to develop
  a second hotel, would require approval by the Planning Commission with a Conditional
  Use Permit and any future submittal to construct an on-premise or off-premise
  freestanding sign would require approval by the Planning Commission with a Sign Use
  Permit. In either scenarios, all the requests mentioned are discretionary applications
  and subject to an environmental review and CEQA determination at the time of their
  submittal.

Discussion

ZC No. 2024-01 is a request to establish the SD 1 overlay. SD 1 is comprised of 11 non-
residential properties, located within the SPA 1, SPA 16, Institutional, and Public Facility overlay
zone districts. SD 1 includes the following parcels listed in no particular order by Assessor Parcel
Numbers: 8047-006-910, 8047-006-922, 8047-006-924, 8047-006-925, 8047-006-926, 8047-
006-927, 8047-007-136, 8047-007-188, 8047-007-189, 8047-007-190 and 8047-007-191. The
proposal meets the minimum site conditions to create a Special Sign District, as set forth in ZTA
No. 2024-02.

ZTA No. 2024-03 proposes to amend Title 17 (Zoning), Chapter 17.01 (Administration), Article
II (Establishment of Zones, and limiting the Uses of Land Therein) and Title 17 (Zoning), Chapter
17.03 (Development Requirements), Article III (Signs) to establish SD 1 development standards
and allow one freeway-oriented on-premise freestanding sign up to 100’ in height. The
development standards specify the maximum freestanding sign height, sign width, number of
sign panels, and sign design review process. There is no implementing project as part of this

request. Any future request to construct a freeway-oriented freestanding sign will require a Sign
Use Permit and the review and approval of the Planning Commission.

The formation of SD 1 will allow business entities within the Norwalk Entertainment District (SPA
16) more flexibility for their signage when submitted as part of their future Master Sign Program.
Additionally, the proposed development standards would allow for a sign height greater than the
existing freestanding sign to maximize freeway visibility.

This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Code of
Regulations, also known as the “Common Sense Exemption” and Section 15311 (Class 11 –
Accessory Structures) of the California Code of Regulations, for the construction or replacement
of minor accessory structures including on-premise signs.

Section 65855 of the California Government Code states that the Planning Commission
shall make a written recommendation on the adoption or amendment of the Zoning
Ordinance.

Section 17.02.260.D of the NMC stipulates that the Planning Commission render its
recommendation on a Zoning Text Amendment, including the reasons for the
recommendation, to the City Council.

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

In 2023, City Council adopted the Norwalk Entertainment District - Civic Center Specific
Plan Area 16 (SPA 16). SPA 16 is located at the southeast corner of Imperial Highway
and Norwalk Boulevard in Norwalk. The development of this area is anticipated to be
implemented through one or more leases to a private developer of all or a portion of the
portion of the City owned land and other contractual arrangements between the City and
a private developer.

The aim of SPA 16 is to advance the City’s goals for the plan area including the Civic
Center as an economic node to enhance the area as a thriving and experience-oriented
center for residents and visitors. SPA 16 capitalizes on the area and its close proximity to
major transportation nodes to establish a vibrant regional destination and draw for the
area. SPA 16 requires the developer to submit a Master Sign Plan for the area which will
allow for flexibility by recognizing the unique aspects of the mixed-use center and need
for various sign types and placement opportunities while ensuring consistency and quality
of design.

Specific Plan Area 1 (SPA 1) is located to the south of SPA 16. The SPA 1 parcels
included in this proposal comprise the AMC Theater, retail pad tenants and the Outback
Steakhouse. Currently there is one existing freestanding sign located in Assessor Parcel
No. 8047-007-191, (the Outback Steakhouse) that would be located within the boundary
of proposed SD 1. The Outback Steakhouse and the City of Norwalk currently have sign
panels on the existing freestanding structure, which was constructed in 1999. The
freestanding sign is 70 feet in height.

The existing height and location of the existing freestanding sign is not optimal given the
existing conditions. Expansions and improvements to Interstate-5 Freeway have
diminished the visibility of the existing freestanding sign. Additionally, the existing sign is
located within the Caltrans right-of- way and is therefore subject to Caltrans requirements
for off-premise signs. Establishing the proposed SD 1 would modify Caltrans authority
and allow for the relocation of the existing on-premise sign with a taller freestanding sign
with a Sign Use Permit. Sign Use Permits require approval by the Planning Commission.

Presented concurrently with this request is ZTA 2024-02, a City staff-initiated request to
amend the Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) to allow for the creation of Special Sign
Districts and establish minimum requirements for those newly created districts. ZTA 2024-
02 amends Chapter 17.02, Article V (Discretionary Approvals and Permits) of the NMC
to enable the creation of Special Sign Districts with specified criteria. These districts
require approval by the City Council, must contain multiple parcels reasonably grouped
together, and meet the following requirements:

  •  Newly created sign districts shall be limited to properties within SPA 1, SPA 16,
  mixed-use, commercial, institutional areas or public facility overlay zones;
  •  Minimum combined land area shall be five (5) acres;
  •  Parcels shall be contiguous (but may be separated by a railroad or public street);
  and
  •  Existing Uses shall include one (1) or more of the following: vehicle sales and lease
  (general new and used), hotels and motels (with 100 or more rooms) or a retail
  tenant (with a minimum of area of 10,000 square feet).
  •  All development standards shall be determined at the time the Special Sign District
  is established and incorporated within the Special Sign District’s Ordinance.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION
Zone Change No. 2024-01 is a request to establish the Special Sign District No. 01 (SD
1) overlay. SD 1 is comprised of 11 non- residential properties, located within in the SPA
1, SPA 16, Institutional and Public Facility overlay zone districts. SD 1 includes the
following parcels listed in no particular order by assessor parcel numbers: 8047-006-910,
8047-006-922, 8047-006-924, 8047-006-925, 8047-006-926, 8047-006-927, 8047-007-
136, 8047-007-188, 8047-007-189, 8047-007-190 and 8047-007-191.

Zoning Text Amendment No. 2024-03 proposes to amend Title 17 (Zoning), Chapter
17.01 (Administration), Article II (Establishment of Zones, and limiting the Uses of Land
Therein) and Title 17 (Zoning), Chapter 17.03 (Development Requirements), Article III
(Signs) to establish SD 1 development standards and allow one freeway-oriented on-
premise freestanding sign greater than 35 feet.

ANALYSIS

Per § 17.03.140 of the NMC, freestanding signs are permitted in the C-1, C-3, C-M, M-1
and M-2 zones, subject to the approval of a sign use permit. Freestanding signs are
limited to a maximum height limit of 35 feet above finished grade, or as otherwise
determined by an approved Sign Use Permit.

The proposed development standards for the on-premise freestanding signs would allow
for a greater height maximum to account for elevation differences between the proposed
sign location and Interstate-5 Freeway. The Interstate-5 Freeway lanes are elevated at
the existing Norwalk Boulevard underpass. Allowing for a 100-foot freestanding sign
would counter the change in elevation and provide adequate exposure for vehicles driving
in the northbound and southbound lanes to view signage along the frontage area. The
proposed SD 1 development standards will allow replacement of the existing on-premise
sign with a taller freestanding sign to advertise uses within the SD 1 boundary.

The formation of a SD 1 will allow businesses entities within the Norwalk Entertainment
District (SPA 16) more flexibility for their signage when submitted as part of their future
Master Sign Program.

ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

The proposed Resolution is exempt by the provisions of the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to Sections 15061(b)(3) of the California Code of
Regulations, also known as the “Common Sense Exemption” and 15311 (Class 11 –
Accessory Structures), for the construction or replacement of minor accessory structures
including on-premise signs. A public notice was prepared and published in the local
newspaper. Four (4) notices were posted on or in proximity to the subject parcels. Any
future project subject to the SD 1 provisions shall undergo its own independent
environmental review for compliance.

SUMMARY

Staff finds the purpose of ZC No. 2024-01 and ZTA No. 2024-03 objectives and standards
in line with the goals and policies of the General Plan and in compliance with the
regulations within the City of Norwalk Municipal Code. Establishing the SD 1 boundary
area, as shown in Attachment A, and the development standards, as shown in Attachment
B, will serve as an effective tool to allow one on-premise freestanding sign oriented
towards the freeway. Such signs are desirable to the City as they provide opportunities
to enhance urban aesthetics and promote effective communication through controlled and
cohesive signage.

  3. WHY IS THE CITY NOT CONSIDERING ADDITIONAL USES—LIKE HOUSING—OR GREATER PROTECTIONS

  Currently, the SPA 1 allows “residential condominiums” in some areas of the SPA 1. (NMC §
  17.09.090; see also Fig. 4 above.) While the ZTA increases flexibility for commercial uses (e.g., hotel,
  retail, entertainment), it does not allow any increased flexibility for residential uses, like allowing
  housing throughout the plan area maximizing affordable housing. Under the City’s recently adopted
  2021-2029 Housing Element (“Housing Element”),15 the City has a Regional Housing Needs
  Allocation (“RHNA”) of approximately 5,000 units, with roughly 60 percent of the units needing to
  be affordable at moderate-income levels or lower. (See Housing Element, p. 175.) In light of the high
  need for housing (particularly affordable), it seems that the City should reconsider the best and
  highest use of the Site—such as a mixed-use housing development. Furthermore, the City should
  consider more protections over hotels, not fewer protections than those minimal limits adopted
  nearly 40 years ago. To address impacts caused by any future hotel project and ensure maximum
  public benefits, the City should consider making hotel use contingent on entering into a hotel-
  specific Development Agreement (“DA”) pursuant to Gov. Code § 65865 et. seq., as done by other
  cities or disallowing hotel use in this area.16

  In conclusion, the proposed ZTA is a project-specific SPA amendment that does not qualify
  for a Common-Sense exemption under CEQA. Local 11 respectfully requests that the Planning
